newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu names respected general to head Zaire army.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu names respected general to head Zaire army.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seseko signed a decree on Wednesday appointing repected general Mahele Bokoungo Lieko in charge of the Zaire army to put troops on a war footing to deal with a Rwandan-backed rebellion, state television said.

In his first act since returning home on Tuesday to deal with the rebellion after four months of medical treatment in Europe, Mobutu shunted aside civil guard commander General Baramoto Kpama, who was appointed chief of army staff only last month.

Military sources said Mahele gave two conditions for taking charge of the demoralised and ill-disciplined army -- control of the entire military command, including the pampered presidential guard, and the power to sanction senior officers. It was not clear if the conditions were granted.
The television said the move was "part of a restructuring of the armed forces of Zaire with the view to putting them on a war footing and improving their efficiency".
Mobutu would meet Zaire's political leaders on Thursday to discuss the crisis following the routing of the army by Rwandan-backed rebels, the television said.

Baramoto was appointed army chief last month after the suspension of General Eleuki Monga for accusing the government of not giving the army the means to deal with the rebellion launched in October by ethnic Tutsis, who have seized territory in the east.
Eleuki had also publicly differed with the government in its call for an international force in Zaire.
Mahele is a veteran of previous military intervention by Zaire into neighbouring Rwanda. He has fought rebel leader Laurent Kabila who heads the guerrilla alliance battling the Zaire army.
Baramoto had been placed "at the disposition of the presidency", with the command of the much feared civil guard passing to little known General Vungbo Ndepo, the television said.
